blocks.content: Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy constitute the conscience of the Constitution.

items: Exams frequently test legal enforceability: Fundamental Rights can be directly enforced under Article 32, whereas Article 37 explicitly makes DPSPs non-justiciable.
Remember the Minerva Mills case (1980) ruling that the Constitution is founded on the bedrock of balance between Part III and Part IV.
Article 31C provides protection to laws implementing Articles 39(b) and 39(c) even if they violate Articles 14 and 19.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fundamental Rights (Part III) are justiciable in court, while Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) are non-justiciable.
Fundamental Rights aim to establish political democracy, whereas DPSPs seek to establish social and economic democracy.
Fundamental Rights place negative obligations on the State, while Directive Principles serve as positive directives for policy formulation.
The Constitution maintains a delicate balance between Part III and Part IV, making them complementary to each other.
